en.title: Output All Pairs with the Minimum Absolute Difference
en.description:
The array elements are distinct. Output all value pairs whose absolute difference is minimal. In each pair the smaller value comes first, and pairs are sorted ascending by the first item and then by the second. The output of the original example [-1,3,6,-5,0] is wrong: the minimum difference is 1, and the only correct value pair is −1 and 0, not the two pairs with difference 3.

The ranges added by this site for missing bounds and the recovery of source typos are described in the input protocol.
en.input: The input gives n and n distinct integers. The original has no numeric bounds; this site adds 2≤n≤100000, −10^9≤a[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output one pair of values with the minimum absolute difference per line, covering all optimal pairs; do not output the number of pairs or the difference.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: -1 0; 1 2 / 2 3 / 3 4; -7 9. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: After sorting, find the minimum difference between adjacent elements, then output in order every adjacent pair that achieves it.
